text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: autoscaler_hit_max_nodes in cluster redwood-prod (auto-pager to #incidents)

alex: saw the alert — queue depth to inference-gpu-q spiked, autoscaler reported max_nodes reached. lots of throttled requests (429s). investigating.

maya: timeline: spike started ~1958001200, queue grew from ~800 -> 12k in ~6m. cluster-autoscaler logs show 'reached max node count'. current maxNodes for pool is 42.

alex: customer impact: AcmeRetail reports timeouts in their checkout AI feature, CS says ~30% of requests are being rate-limited. jamie, can you confirm customer-facing severity? :eyes:

jamie: confirmed customer on live campaign, they are seeing errors and single-digit % revenue impact so far but trending up. urgent.

maya: root cause hypothesis: a combination of a sudden workload burst + some pods not evicting fast due to podDisruptionBudget + horizontal pod autoscaler (HPA) capped by maxNodes -> unschedulable pods piling up. logs show many Pending pods with error '0/42 nodes are available'.

alex: can we do a temporary manual increase of node pool ceiling while we investigate autoscaler policy? would like a short bump to 55 nodes for 30m to let backlog drain.

cher: cost/approval: short bump OK from my side for emergency mitigation. please document in thread. :thumbsup:

maya: steps to request manual override: 1) check org quota with cloud console 2) patch cluster-autoscaler config or use cloud resize 3) watch pending pods become scheduled.

alex: checking quotas now.

tony: I can run the resize. confirming we have quota headroom in account (compute cores and GPUs). I'm also going to disable the cluster-autoscaler scale-down quickly to avoid oscillation.

maya: suggested commands (GKE example):

```bash
# increase node pool max via gcloud (imperative)
gcloud container clusters resize redwood-prod --node-pool=redwood-inference-pool --num-nodes=55 --project=redwood-prod --zone=us-central1-a

# or patch autoscaler config (declarative)
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap cluster-autoscaler-status --patch '{"data":{"max_nodes":"55"}}'
```

alex: note: also check HPA maxReplicas and pod resource requests, cheap wins: lower per-pod CPU request to allow scheduling if safe.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline blocked: awaiting infra changes (automations paused).

tony: running resize now. will post back when node group update completes. ETA ~3-7m.

(3m)

tony: resize command accepted, nodes provisioning. I see new instances hitting provisioning steps.

(6m)

tony: nodes entered Ready, kube-scheduler is assigning pods. Pending count dropping: 11. queue depth still high but decreasing.

alex: monitoring metrics: queued inference requests down from 12k -> 1.2k in 4m. 429 rate dropped by 90%.

jamie: confirmed AcmeRetail reporting errors gone, their telemetry shows successful requests returning to normal.

maya: follow-up: we need to (a) adjust cluster-autoscaler maxNodes upward in config to persist above 55 until we finish a safe autoscaler tuning, (b) investigate why HPA and PDB interplay caused backlog spike, (c) add guardrails in runbook for manual bump + cost tags.

cher: agree. create a post-incident ticket and add to next-oncall rotation review.

alex: i'm going to mark this mitigation successful. keeping the pool at 55 for 1h to ensure no second wave. will document commands run and timeline here.

alex: commands run (summary):

```
# imperative resize (GKE)
gcloud container clusters resize redwood-prod --node-pool=redwood-inference-pool --num-nodes=55 --zone=us-central1-a

# temporarily disable scale-down
kubectl -n kube-system annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler redwood-keep-warm=\"true\"
```

tony: leaving monitoring alerts on for queue growth and node provisioning failures. I'll revert to original maxNodes after postmortem-approved timeframe.

jamie: notified account and AM. customer slack thread updated.

alex: postmortem action items (short):
- autoscaler: review maxNodes defaults and autoscaler policy for bursty inference workloads
- HPA & PDB: add test scenarios for eviction/scheduling under burst
- runbook: add clear manual bump checklist + approval matrix and terraform/gcloud playbook
- cost controls: tagging and temporary-cost-notification to finance

maya: adding a note: consider adding a 'burst' emergency quota autoscaler for critical tenants to avoid cross-tenant impact.

cher: thanks team. closing the incident when postmortem ticket created. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident resolved by manual node pool increase, mitigation timestamp 1958001710. Incident duration ~10m from pager to mitigation.

alex: thread summary posted to #postmortems after ticket created. Good job everyone.
